answer: An AI-agent marketplace requires each seller, whether planning a terrace, tracking a falcon, or tending a lotus pond, to escrow collateral equal to the value of its open contracts. A contract automatically slashes that bond if the seller misses a delivery deadline recorded on-chain. Splitting into a thousand identities creates no extra unsecured capacity: the attacker must fund every alias’s contracts, tie up capital, and lose collateral on defaults.
